Fewer abandoned sign-ups, verified merchants and queues analysts trust

For payment aggregators, wallet and PPI issuers, neo-banking apps and digital lending platforms, we connect product events, onboarding, dispute and risk systems so stalled sign-ups get timely help, merchants are verified before going live, disputes meet their deadlines and fraud alerts reach an analyst with the evidence attached.

What makes fintech & payments different

  • Users abandon sign-up at KYC, bank linking or mandate setup, and generic reminder blasts annoy more than they help.

  • RBI's September 2025 payment aggregator directions require merchant due diligence before activation, from full KYC to contact point verification for small merchants, and good merchants wait while checks run by hand.

  • Chargebacks and UPI disputes arrive from several portals with hard deadlines, and the evidence sits across ledgers, merchants and support tickets.

  • Fraud rules raise more alerts than analysts can review, and the context they need lives in several different tools.

Where automation helps fintech & payments

  • Drop-off recovery by stall reason

    Users who stall at KYC, bank linking or mandate setup get one helpful message for their specific problem, and repeated failures go to support with the event trail attached.

  • Merchant onboarding and risk tiering

    Document collection, PAN, GSTIN, bank account and website checks, risk tiers agreed with your risk team, and an approval console so no merchant goes live before due diligence.

  • Dispute and chargeback queue

    Card chargebacks, UPI disputes and failed-transaction complaints in one queue with deadlines, evidence collected automatically and AI-drafted responses for analysts to edit.

  • Fraud alert triage

    Alerts enriched with device, velocity and linked-account context, summarized and prioritized for analysts, with every decision recorded to tune the rules.

  • Digital lending platform journeys

    For lending apps and LSPs: indicative eligibility, a neutral view of partner lender offers, and EMI reminders and bounce handling designed around RBI's Digital Lending Directions.

Discover and inquireStandard3–5 weeks

Inquiry desk with indicative eligibility

Capture loan inquiries from ads, aggregators, the website, WhatsApp and DSAs, ask only what indicative eligibility needs, check it against the lender's published criteria, and route likely applicants to the right owner. It guides; it never decides.

Lending & NBFCs · Fintech & payments

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Loan inquiries arrive from campaigns, aggregators, DSAs and WhatsApp in different formats. Many fall outside the lender's serviceable areas or product rules, while good prospects wait hours for a callback and apply elsewhere. Sales staff sometimes over-promise approval or rates, which turns into complaints and mis-selling risk later.

Trigger

A new inquiry from a lead form, the lender's WhatsApp Business number, website chat, an aggregator feed or a DSA submission.

How it runs

  1. Capture the inquiry into one queue with source, product interest and the consent shown at that step. AI reads free-text messages for product and amount, and duplicates of existing customers or open applications are merged.
  2. Collect a short set of banded answers on a page on the lender's domain: pincode, product, amount range, age band, employment type and income band. No PAN, Aadhaar or bank details are requested at this stage.
  3. Check the answers against the lender's published criteria, such as serviceable pincodes, age, minimum income and product limits, and show a plainly worded result with the reason.
  4. Route likely applicants to the branch, relationship manager, DSA owner or digital application journey by product and location, with a summary of what was shared.
  5. On multi-lender platforms, display every matching offer that partner lenders return, with each lender's name, amount, tenor, APR and charges, without favoring any lender, as the Digital Lending Directions require.
  6. Send one approved follow-up template to opted-in prospects who have not applied, then close the inquiry with a reason code.

Human checkpoint

Indicative results never promise approval, a rate or a limit. Credit assessment, bureau checks and the decision stay with the lender's credit team after a full application, and sales staff take over whenever the prospect asks for a person or the case is unusual.

Only sales and credit roles can see them.

What we deliver

  • Indicative eligibility rules agreed with credit and compliance

How we measure it

  • Inquiry-to-application conversion by source
  • Share of inquiries outside serviceable criteria
  • Mis-selling complaints traced to the inquiry stage

Apply, verify and decideStandard3–5 weeks

Onboarding drop-off recovery for apps

Detect where users stall in sign-up, such as KYC, bank linking or mandate setup, identify the likely reason, and send one helpful, consented nudge or route the user to support instead of sending blanket reminders.

Fintech & payments

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Wallets, neo-banking and lending apps lose many users between sign-up and first use. Generic reminder blasts ignore why someone stopped, such as a failed Video KYC call, a PAN-name mismatch or a bank verification error, and they irritate users who have given up or asked not to be contacted.

Trigger

A product event shows that a user has not completed an onboarding step within the agreed time, or that a step has failed.

How it runs

  1. Stream onboarding events from the app into an analytics store, with each user's consent and channel preferences attached.
  2. Classify the stall: not started, document problem, Video KYC missed or failed, bank verification failure, mandate not set up, or technical error.
  3. Send one helpful message for that reason by push, email or an approved WhatsApp template where the user opted in, with a resume link and a support option, within frequency caps.
  4. Route repeated failures and technical errors to support with the event trail, so agents never ask the user to start again.
  5. Stop all nudges once the user completes the step, opts out or closes the account, and report recovery by step and cohort.

Human checkpoint

Onboarding operations and compliance handle every KYC exception and decide edge cases. Product owners approve every message and frequency cap, and nudges never promise credit, limits or rewards outside approved terms.

Apply, verify and decideAdvanced6–9 weeks

Merchant onboarding and due diligence queue

Collect merchant documents, run checks on PAN, GSTIN, bank account and website, assign a risk tier, and give onboarding officers one queue, so no merchant goes live before due diligence is complete and approved.

Fintech & payments

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Under RBI's September 2025 payment aggregator directions, PAs must complete merchant due diligence before activation, with full KYC for most merchants and contact point verification for small ones, and most also screen websites for prohibited goods and missing refund policies. Manual checks across email, spreadsheets and vendor dashboards slow good merchants and let incomplete files slip through.

Trigger

A merchant submits the sign-up form, a sales partner refers a merchant, or an existing merchant's re-KYC falls due.

How it runs

  1. Collect business details and documents by merchant type on a secure onboarding page, with consent and purpose shown.
  2. Run verification through approved vendors: PAN, GSTIN, bank account validation, CKYC where available, and Video KYC or contact point verification where policy requires it.
  3. Scan the merchant's website or app listing with AI for refund, cancellation and contact policies, and for product categories the PA does not serve, for an officer to confirm.
  4. Assign a risk tier from business category, expected volumes and check results, using rules agreed with the risk team.
  5. Present the file in an onboarding console where officers approve, request more information or reject; higher tiers go to risk or compliance.
  6. Activate only after approval, send the merchant clear status updates, and schedule re-KYC and monitoring by tier.

Human checkpoint

Onboarding officers approve or reject every merchant, and risk or compliance approves higher-risk tiers. Automated checks inform the decision; they never activate a merchant on their own.

Systems it connects

  • PA onboarding portal and merchant database
  • PAN, GSTIN and bank verification APIs
  • CKYC and Video KYC vendors

Uses business and beneficial owner KYC data, bank details and website content. Data is stored encrypted on systems in India with role-based access and kept for the record-keeping period KYC and PMLA rules set, and payment data is stored only in India, as RBI requires.

What we deliver

  • Verification integrations and website scan
  • Risk-tiering rules agreed with risk and compliance
  • Onboarding console with audit trail

How we measure it

  • Files approved without rework
  • Merchants activated before approval, with a target of none
  • Re-KYC completed on schedule

Pay and renewStandard4–6 weeks

EMI reminders and respectful collections workflow

Remind borrowers before each EMI, flag mandate bounces the same day, and run overdue follow-up through approved channels within RBI's conduct rules, with hardship cases routed to a trained officer.

Lending & NBFCs · Fintech & payments

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Bounced NACH and UPI AutoPay debits surface late, reminders go out from dialer lists that ignore preferences and contact hours, and early-stage overdue customers get the same treatment as wilful defaulters. That raises complaints and conduct risk without improving recovery.

Trigger

A daily sync of installments due in the coming days from the LMS API or export, and mandate presentation results from the sponsor bank or payment gateway.

How it runs

  1. Send pre-due reminders in the borrower's language with amount, date and payment options by DLT SMS, email, app notification, or an approved WhatsApp utility template where the borrower opted in, with no offers that would make them promotional.
  2. Detect bounced debits the same day and send a factual notice by DLT SMS, email or app notification with a payment link on the lender's domain and charges as set in the loan agreement.
  3. Run overdue follow-up by SMS, email, app and calls from 1600-series numbers, since WhatsApp's policy lists debt collection as a prohibited use, and schedule calls only between 8 am and 7 pm, or narrower hours where rules or borrower preferences require.
  4. Flag hardship signals, such as job loss, illness or bereavement, and route them to a trained officer to discuss options under the lender's policy.
  5. When a recovery agent is assigned or changed, send the borrower the agent's details by SMS and email before any contact, and from January 2027 confirm the agent's certification first.
  6. Log every attempt, outcome and recording reference, and report any contact outside the rules to the collections head the same day.

Human checkpoint

Collections officers decide settlements, restructuring, waivers, agent assignment and any legal step. The workflow never threatens, never contacts relatives or references, and never sends legal notices on its own.

Claims, disputes and alertsAdvanced6–9 weeks

Dispute and chargeback operations queue

Bring card chargebacks, UPI disputes and failed-transaction complaints into one queue with deadlines, gather evidence automatically from ledgers and merchants, and give analysts a drafted response to review before anything is submitted.

Fintech & payments

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Disputes arrive through acquirer and card network portals, NPCI's dispute system, merchant emails and support tickets, each with its own reason codes and deadlines. Analysts copy data between tools, evidence requests reach merchants late, and missed deadlines become automatic losses or compensation for delayed failed-transaction reversals.

Trigger

A new chargeback, UPI dispute or failed-transaction complaint arrives from a network portal, the sponsor or acquiring bank, or the helpdesk.

How it runs

  1. Normalize each dispute into a case with transaction, reason code, amount, merchant and the response deadline that applies.
  2. Pull evidence automatically: ledger and settlement records, authentication results, refund history, delivery or service proof and past disputes.
  3. Request missing evidence from the merchant with a deadline and reminders, listing what that reason code needs.
  4. Draft a representment summary with AI from the evidence pack for the analyst to edit.
  5. The analyst accepts, represents or refunds; failed-transaction reversals and any compensation follow RBI's turnaround time rules.
  6. Track deadlines and outcomes by network, reason code and merchant, and pass repeat patterns to the risk team.

Human checkpoint

Dispute analysts decide every acceptance, representment and refund, and finance approves write-offs. Nothing is submitted to a network or bank without an analyst's approval.

Claims, disputes and alertsAdvanced6–10 weeks

Fraud alert triage for analysts

Enrich every fraud or risk alert with customer, device and transaction context, summarize the evidence, prioritize the queue by severity and time sensitivity, and record each analyst decision to improve the rules.

Fintech & payments · Lending & NBFCs

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Rules and models raise more alerts than analysts can clear, and each review means opening the core system, device logs, past cases and KYC files. Urgent cases, such as an account takeover in progress or a mule account receiving funds, wait behind low-risk noise, and decisions are rarely recorded well enough to improve the rules.

Trigger

An alert from transaction monitoring, the risk engine or early warning signals on loans, or a fraud complaint received through the cybercrime reporting system.

How it runs

  1. Enrich the alert with account age, KYC status, device and login history, velocity, beneficiaries and linked accounts.
  2. Summarize the evidence with AI in a fixed format and suggest a priority with reasons, citing the data used.
  3. Queue alerts by severity and time sensitivity, and page the on-call analyst for alerts that need action within minutes.
  4. The analyst decides: release, contact the customer through a verified channel, hold or block within policy, or escalate to the fraud risk unit.
  5. Record the decision and reason, trigger customer messages from approved templates, and pass reportable cases to the officers who own fraud reporting and suspicious transaction reports.
  6. Review outcomes weekly with the risk team to retire noisy rules and adjust thresholds.

Human checkpoint

Fraud analysts decide every hold, block, release and escalation. Classifying a borrower account as fraud follows the lender's board-approved process, including the borrower's right to be heard, and fraud reports to the regulator and suspicious transaction reports to FIU-IND stay with the responsible officers.
